thread.title: Apple’s Tim Cook says regulatory action is needed to restore ‘full faith’ in tech - MarketWatch

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple’s Tim Cook says regulatory action is needed to restore ‘full faith’ in tech - MarketWatch
text:
Apple Inc. Chief Executive Tim Cook has extended his crusade against companies that misuse user data, calling in a Thursday op-ed written for Time for “comprehensive federal privacy legislation”:
‘Consumers shouldn’t have to tolerate another year of companies irresponsibly amassing huge user profiles, data breaches that seem out of control and the vanishing ability to control our own digital lives.’ Tim Cook, Apple The Apple AAPL, +0.32% CEO laid out the components he believes are necessary for regulators to consider if they set out to create effective privacy laws. These include the ability for users to know which data are being collected on them as well as how to access and delete this information. He also called on companies to strip personal information from customer data or not collect it at all.
“Technology has the potential to keep changing the world for the better, but it will never achieve that potential without the full faith and confidence of the people who use it,” he wrote.

Cook suggested that the federal government create a “data-broker clearinghouse” that would make all parties that sell user data register with the government. This would let users track transactions that have led to their data being sold and also let them delete this identifying information “once and for all.”
The comments in the Time op-ed follow months of criticism by Cook directed toward tech peers. Following Facebook Inc.’s FB, +0.00% Cambridge Analytica scandal, the Apple chief said he “wouldn’t be in this situation” when an interviewer asked him what he would do if he were at the helm of Facebook. Cook has repeatedly contrasted Apple’s stance on data sharing with that of Facebook and others.
Read more: Apple CEO Tim Cook has some harsh words for Facebook
“The truth is, we could make a ton of money if we monetized our consumer, if our consumer was our product,” Cook said at the time, according to Recode . “We’ve elected not to do that.”
Apple shares are down 0.5% in Thursday trading. The stock has fallen 30% in the past three months, as the , of which Apple is a component, has slipped 6%.
Emily Bary Emily Bary is a MarketWatch reporter based in New
